facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections for the past 5 years
He denied hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
No prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma were reported
Nasal endoscopy revealed destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, along with purulent, yellow drainage and crusting
C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, white blood cell count, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel results were normal
HIV test was negative
Axial and coronal scans reveal a substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate
Shows thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses, erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system
Chest CT: Showed enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum
Sinus mucosa showed noncaseating granulomas
AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node was positive
Culture showed growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas

He denied hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
No prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma were reported
Nasal endoscopy revealed destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, along with purulent, yellow drainage and crusting
C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, white blood cell count, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel results were normal
HIV test was negative
Axial and coronal scans reveal a substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate
Shows thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses, erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system
Chest CT: Showed enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum

concepts.why: The presence of noncaseating granulomas in the sinus mucosa and the growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas suggest a chronic granulomatous infection.
The presence of noncaseating granulomas in the sinus mucosa and the positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node suggest sarcoidosis, which is a systemic granulomatous disease.
The presence of destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, and the erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system, suggest Wegener's granulomatosis, which is a form of vasculitis.
The positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node suggests tuberculosis, which is a chronic bacterial infection.
The growth of Staphylococcus aureus in the culture suggests staphylococcal sinusitis, which is a type of bacterial infection.
The growth of Pseudomonas in the culture suggests pseudomonal sinusitis, which is a type of bacterial infection.

The presence of destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, and the erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system, suggest allergic fungal sinusitis, which is a type of immune-mediated disease.
The negative HIV test and the presence of recurrent sinus infections suggest sinusitis due to immune deficiency, which is a type of immune-mediated disease.
It explains the substantial septal deformity and near complete destruction of the sinus septate found in the imaging studies.
